column1: # CP13 prevalidation rules, each decided against legacy (rules_test.py).
# Integration (feature-site-dx in the base): an unterminated quote or `[` that
# reaches the end of its block is a translator error in legacy and in the CP10
# splitter (earliest unterminated opener wins), so those rows are now
# `reject translator fails` (were R1/R2 with legacy silent).
# context: top = between print("a") and print("b"); dead = inside if(0 == 1) {...};
# after-return = after `return 0` in a called function; fn = inside a function that
# IS called; uncalled = inside a function that is never called (legacy never
# translates/evaluates it: these are the D-022 #3 "before anything runs" cases).

column5: k := (v) => { fn add(a) { return a } }; k(1)

column1: # Owner addition (2): syntactically valid programs that fail at run time are
# accepted - at top level and in code that never runs (dead branches,
# D-025: multi-line return values (\n = line break). Continuation only inside
# a bracket the value opened; a never-closed bracket is still R2.
# Integration (CP13 phase A certify finding): commas in the arguments of a
# call whose callee is not a function declared in the unit (a method, a
# built-in, any other name) and in function signatures are not R3: legacy
# reports the callee's arity error when the call runs, or the translator's
# Integration (CP13 phase A certify regression, 0b879df6): `?[` is one
# token (optional index) and opens like `[`; `?.` is a member link. Optional
# access on a literal or parenthesised receiver is Opaque in the CP10 parser
# (legacy decides), so these statements are exactly the regions the
# prevalidator inspects (an unclosed `?[` is the translator's, as `[`). Defer
# rule: an R2 finding stands only when the raw characters are unbalanced too.
